question: Carmen needs $7 more to have twice the amount of money that Jethro has. Meanwhile, Patricia has $60, which is 3 times as much as Jethro. What is the sum of all their money?
solution:
Jethro has 60/3 = $<<60/3=20>>20.
Twice of what Jethro has is $20 x 2 = $40
Carmen has $40 - 7 = $<<40-7=33>>33
The sum of all their money is $60 + $20 + $33 = $<<60+20+33=113>>113
#### 113

Let C be the amount of money Carmen has.
Let J be the amount of money Jethro has.
Let P be the amount of money Patricia has.

We are given that Carmen needs $7 more to have twice the amount of money that Jethro has. This can be written as:
C + 7 = 2J

We are also given that Patricia has $60, so P = 60.
We are given that Patricia has 3 times as much as Jethro, so P = 3J.
Therefore, 60 = 3J, which implies J = 60/3 = 20.

Now we can substitute J = 20 into the equation C + 7 = 2J:
C + 7 = 2(20)
C + 7 = 40
C = 40 - 7
C = 33

The sum of all their money is C + J + P = 33 + 20 + 60 = 113.
